to change written or spoken words into another language
Example: somebody has offered to translate  my blog into Spanish and Japanese.
These are words you use to talk about communications.
someone who changes a piece of writing into a different language
Example: If I had thought of it earlier, I could've told you about a translator.
a statement which does not seem to be connected in a reasonable or sensible way with what was said before
Example: What does that have to do with anything? You are the king of non sequiturs!
to change the date or time of a planned event or action to a later one
Example: If I had known everyone was going to be so stressed and touchy I would've postponed tonight's dinner.
feeling very worried, annoyed  or anxious
to make someone feel interested in something
Example: Weren't you going to tell us something earlier? You've piqued my curiosity.
Go online and find 8 to 10 minimal pairs with I and e (disk and desk).
Write down the minimal pairs and practice them with a partner.
Write a poem using as many of the minimal pairs as you can.
I find minimal pairs (I and e) online.
I practice minimal pairs with a partner.
I write using minimal pairs in a poem.
Minimal Pairs are two words that sound similar, except for one sound.
The vowel sounds i and e are hard to distinguish for non-native speakers. They are “close together” in terms of position of tongue and lips.
To make the sound i sound, your tongue is slightly raised off the bottom of your mouth. It rests behind your teeth, but doesn't touch them. It is a voiced sound.
Say the word miss. Say each sound separately, focusing on the short i sound: m - i - s.
To make the sound e sound, your tongue is slightly higher in your mouth than i. You mouth is also shaped in a smile. Look in the mirror as you say the short e sound.
Say the word mess. Say each sound separately, focusing on the short e sound: m - e -s.
Here are a list of minimal pairs with the i and the e sounds. As you read them, focus on the difference between the two sounds.
Well looks like you missed the boat, again! What a mess!
I thought I'd do the cooking so you could set the table. We can all sit down now.
Well, will you clean it up before we sit down?
I didn't plug my phone in. Now it's dead.
I won't tell you till after we eat.
Reduction of Have in Past Modals and of Auxiliary Verbs
When you use auxiliary verbs like have, it is common to reduce it in conversation. </br></br>  In English, not every word or syllable is pronounced fully.
When you reduce the sound of have it sounds like uv or iv.
Read each sentence in it's full form:

I should have thought of it before.
I could have told you about a translator.
You could have told me you were cooking bacon.
I would have done it.
I would have postponed tonight's dinner.
Now read them and reduce the pronunciation of the auxiliary verb have:

I should've thought of it before. should_uv
I could've told you about a translator. could_uv
You could've told me you were cooking bacon. could_uv
I would've done it. would_uv
I would've postponed tonight's dinner. would_uv
I can talk about emotions, opinions, behavior and work.
I can say and use words like disk and desk.
I can say and use could've and would've.

Sally: Guess what guys my blog has become so popular, somebody has offered to translate it into Spanish and Japanese! I should have thought of it before.
Peter: If I had thought of it earlier, I could have told you about a translator.
Vanessa: Well looks like you missed the boat, again! What a mess! You could have told me you were cooking bacon.
Sally: I thought I'd do the cooking so you could set the table. We can all sit down now.
Vanessa: Well, will you clean it up before we sit down?
Sally: Sorry, if I had known there was a better way to cook bacon, I would have done it.

Peter: I didn't plug my phone in. Now it's dead.
Sally: What does that have to do with anything? You are the king of non sequiturs!
Peter: I won't tell you till after we eat.
Vanessa: Such a man of mystery.
Sally: If I had known everyone was going to be so stressed and touchy I would have postponed tonight's dinner.

Peter: So people will be reading your blog globally now? That's pretty great.
Sally: Weren't you going to tell us something earlier? You've piqued my curiosity.
Vanessa: Yes, why does it matter that your phone is dead? Did you expect someone special to call?
Peter: As a matter of fact I, do. Now here's to a good meal!
Sally and Vanessa: Ooooh
